findings.failing_input: When the cron runs at 23:59 IL on day D and the function is invoked with dateStr='D' (today), `dayInTz(new Date().toISOString(), SHOPIFY_TZ)` returns 'D' and `nextDayStr` returns 'D+1', so updated_at_max = midnight of D+1. Then between 23:59 and 00:00, the cron rollover happens. If the same function is re-invoked at 00:00:30 with dateStr='D' (intentional backfill), `dayInTz(new Date())` returns 'D+1' and `nextDayStr` returns 'D+2', so updated_at_max = midnight of D+2. This is correct behavior (open-ended to today+1).
findings.expected: Open-ended window grows daily, including current day.
findings.actual: Correct. No bug. This is the intentional fix from 2026-05-21.

findings.failing_input: Backfilling a date 6 months in the past: Window B = [D, today+1) means we fetch ALL orders updated since D 6 months ago. That can easily blow the PAGINATION_CAP (50 × 250 = 12,500 orders).
findings.expected: PAGINATION_CAP would be hit; warning emitted; algorithm runs on partial data.
findings.actual: Documented in docstring ('Cost grows linearly with backfill depth (~250 orders/day for these stores), bounded by PAGINATION_CAP (50 pages = 12,500 orders), which covers ~50 days of typical store volume'). For deeper backfills, data loss is silent (only console.warn fires). With 3 stores at ~30 orders/day, 6-month backfill = 5,400 orders well under the cap. Acceptable for current operator workflow.
findings.fix_sketch: Could narrow Window B to [D, D+30) (30-day refund window covers >99% of Shopify refunds per docs) instead of all-the-way-to-today. Trade-off: lose any >30-day-old refund attribution. Document.
findings.regression_test_idea: Test backfilling 6-month-old date, mock 51 paginated responses, assert console.warn fires.

findings.failing_input: Window A returns order X with one set of refunds. Window B returns order X with a DIFFERENT (more up-to-date) set of refunds (because updated_at advanced). Code uses `merged.set(key, o)` first for A, then `if (!merged.has(key))` for B — Window A wins.
findings.expected: More recent / authoritative refund set should win.
findings.actual: Comment on line 538 says 'in practice both windows return identical payloads for an overlapping order — Shopify returns the same record, not a windowed view'. This is true: Shopify returns the FULL order record regardless of which window matched. So both A and B contain the same refunds[] (the current state). Window A winning is fine.
findings.fix_sketch: n/a — current behavior is correct given Shopify's API semantics.
findings.regression_test_idea: Pin Shopify's behavior with a test: same orderId in both windows, both return identical refunds[] — assert algorithm gets called with deduped (1 instance).

findings.failing_input: DST transition day in Asia/Jerusalem (March/October). The function iterates 3 times to converge.
findings.expected: Returns correct offset (+02:00 or +03:00 depending on DST).
findings.actual: Test 1b explicitly guards the May case (+03:00 IDT). DST transition day on October 2026 (Asia/Jerusalem switches IDT→IST) is NOT covered by any test. The Date.UTC month-indexing fix on line 299 is critical (commented as the 2026-05-22 incident).
findings.fix_sketch: Add a test for October 31, 2026 (last Sunday of October) or November 1 (first day of IST) where offset should be +02:00.

findings.failing_input: Order with 100% discount (free gift): all items have price=0, subtotal=0. Code path uses flat-spread: totalCad / items.length. If totalCad is also 0 (free gift with no shipping/tax), each line gets 0.
findings.actual: Correct. `useFlatSpread = !(subtotal > 0)` correctly triggers the flat-spread branch. `totalCad / items.length` with items.length > 0 is finite.
findings.regression_test_idea: Test computeLineItemsCad with all-zero prices and totalCad=0 → assert allocations are all 0 (not NaN).

findings.failing_input: Order with utm_source='tiktok' AND utm_medium='cpc' AND source_name='fb' AND fbclid present. The decision tree at lines 878-924 evaluates source_name first → 'meta-paid'.
findings.expected: Documented priority: source_name > click-id > UTM > referrer.
findings.actual: Correct per documented priority. Tested by Test 2 (source_name=fb wins).
findings.regression_test_idea: Adversarial test with conflicting signals across all 4 tiers.

findings.failing_input: utm_medium = 'CPC' (uppercase). Regex `/cpc|paid|paidsocial|social/i` with `i` flag matches case-insensitively → 'paid' branch triggered. Correct.
Shopify defines multiple non-collectible statuses: 'voided', 'cancelled', 'refunded'. Current filter only drops 'voided'. A fully refunded order with financial_status='refunded' is still counted.
findings.expected: Refunded orders should arguably be excluded from order-attribution count (or the totalCad should already be net of refunds via current_total_price).
findings.actual: Code uses `o.current_total_price` (already net of same-day refunds per Shopify). So a fully refunded same-day order has current_total_price=0 and gets counted as an order with $0 totalCad. Acceptable but inconsistent with how Shopify.gs handles it (need to verify Apps Script parity).
findings.fix_sketch: Either document that refunded orders are intentionally kept (with current_total_price reflecting refund net) OR add `o.financial_status === 'refunded'` to the skip list.
findings.regression_test_idea: Test with `financial_status='refunded'` and `current_total_price='0'` and assert it appears in output with totalCad=0.

findings.failing_input: fetchShopifyDayRows calls getShopifyAccessToken at line 592 (per-store). fetchShopifyProductsCatalog/fetchShopifyOrdersAttribution call it via getShopifyCreds. The shopifyAuth module caches tokens; concurrent invocations for the same store across cron functions could both miss-and-refresh. shopifyAuth.ts review will verify.
findings.expected: Token cache shared across invocations within a single Inngest function.

uncertainty_notes: File is 1090 LOC with 3 public fetchers (day rows, catalog, orders-attribution) + extensive helpers. Test file is 824 LOC with 28+ tests covering pagination, Link parsing, DST/TZ (the 2026-05-22 +747:00 incident fix is locked in), Window A vs B merge, dedup, algorithm delegation gate (Test 7), catalog pagination, orders-attribution classification including TikTok branches. Audit snapshot row 5 says 'FULL coverage'. The Window B open-ended fix is critical and tested. Verdict ✅. SVC-08 is the only non-defense finding worth tracking.
